answer: Sybil defence here rests on a bond: each agent that votes or earns must lock a stake, and any agent challenged on identity posts a bond slashed if one key is proven to control several rewarded accounts. An attacker cannot let fake agents wander into the registry for free, since every copy needs its own deposit plus slash risk, so N duplicates cost N deposits at once. Even one ember of proof of shared control burns the whole bond, so each fake account is a near-certain loss, not a pearl of cheap votes, and expected profit turns negative.
